name: Sunghong Park
institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
description: Sunghong Park researches graph learning, domain adaptation, and biomedical AI at KAIST, connecting heterogeneous data for disease diagnosis and biomarker discovery.
intro: I develop machine learning methods that connect heterogeneous data, learn with limited labels, and bring biological structure into biomedical AI.
biography: I am a postdoctoral researcher at the Life Science Research Institute, KAIST. My research connects graph representation learning, semi-supervised learning, and domain adaptation with biomedical problems, including dementia subtyping, longitudinal prediction, and biomarker discovery. I received my Ph.D. in Artificial Intelligence from Ajou University, advised by Professor Hyunjung Shin, and previously conducted postdoctoral research at Ajou University School of Medicine.

research.title: Graph representation learning
research.description: Learning from relationships, not just individual observations. I study graph-based and semi-supervised methods that use network structure when labels are scarce.
research.question: How can multiple relationships support learning when supervision is limited?

research.title: Explainable biomedical AI
research.description: Connecting neuroimaging, plasma proteomics, and biological knowledge to study disease heterogeneity and interpretable biomarkers.
research.question: How can biological structure make multimodal predictions more interpretable?

research.title: Learning across domains & time
research.description: Transferring information between heterogeneous populations, measurement settings, and time points while preserving useful differences.
research.question: What should be shared—and what should be preserved—across domains?
